correctness.rationale: For each coordinate, four real numbers summing to zero obey ∑_(i<j)(a_i−a_j)^4=4∑a_i^4+3(∑a_i²)²; the assigned verify.py expands this identity symbolically. Summation over coordinates of the admissible centered ℓ4-unit vectors gives ∑_(i<j)||x_i−x_j||₄⁴=16+3T with T=4+2∑_(i<j)∑_k x_i(k)²x_j(k)²≤16 by Cauchy and each unit fourth norm. Six-term Cauchy gives (∑_(i<j)||x_i−x_j||₄²)²≤6×64. The explicit four tetrahedral vectors supported on three coordinates, of signed coordinates ±3^(−1/4) with even sign parity, sum to zero, each have unit fourth norm and all six distances have fourth power 32/3, so equality gives 8√6. Summability of all sums for arbitrary I follows from Hölder and finite four-vector support of the argument; three coordinates suffice for sharpness. The exact published planar ℓ4² value 8(1+√2) is strictly smaller because 6>(1+√2)².
